newsitem.title: USA: Mayor of St. Louis defeated in primary.
newsitem.headline: Mayor of St. Louis defeated in primary.

text.p: First-term Mayor Freeman Bosley Jr. was defeated Tuesday in the city's Democratic mayoral primary by former police chief Clarence Harmon, according to exit polls and early returns.
Winning the party primary is equivalent to election in St. Louis, which has not chosen a Republican mayor since 1945. The general election is April 1.
The hard-fought Bosley-Harmon contest had a racial overtones. Both men are black -- Bosley the city's first black mayor and Harmon the first of his race to be the city's police chief.
But some black groups questioned Harmon's record as chief and cast him as a white establishmemnt choice.
Bosley, 47, a former city circuit clerk, was elected mayor in 1993.

The head of the St. Louis Urban League said on the eve of the election that the contest was really "about power" gained by blacks four years ago with Bosley's election and the loss of the same that a Harmon win would yield.
The 57-year-old Harmon in 1991 became the first black chief in the 130-year history of the police department. He retired in 1995 after 27 years with the police department.

During his time as chief the local chapter of the National Association for the Advancement of Coloured People said the police department had a double standard that treated white police better than black.
Returns and exit polls indicated Harmon would win by a 60-40 margin.
